topic: What interference mitigation techniques are viable for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations?
consensus_response: The viable interference mitigation techniques for overlapping service transmissions across geographically dispersed ground stations are Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA), Linear Equalizers based on Kalman filtering, Adaptive frequency allocation, Variable frequency reuse factors, and TDMA-based multiple access schemes. These techniques can be integrated to enhance performance and mitigate various sources of interference, ultimately improving system capacity and reducing mutual interference between aeronautical and terrestrial wireless communications. The integration of Rate Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) with Linear Equalizers based on Kalman filtering can effectively mitigate both multipath and co-channel interference, while Adaptive frequency allocation and Variable frequency reuse factors can minimize interference between ground stations. TDMA-based multiple access schemes can manage channel access and reduce multiple access interference. The proposed techniques can be adapted to diverse international standards and specific implementations across global airports, ensuring high integrity transmission in safety-critical aeronautical applications.
reference_context: The reference context highlights various interference sources, including multipath, co-channel, multiple access, and mutual interference, which can be mitigated using techniques such as rate splitting, common message decoding, linear equalizers, and multiser detection schemes. The context also emphasizes the importance of preventing mutual interference between aeronautical and terrestrial wireless communications, particularly in high-density traffic environments near airports.
